guard_streams.source: Broadband speeds: what you need to know

facts.detail: The Broadband Speeds Code requires clear speed information when a broadband service is purchased.
Customers should receive an estimate for busy periods, defined as 8–10pm for homes and 12–2pm for businesses.
Participating providers should give a personalised minimum guaranteed speed.
If a network speed problem cannot be fixed within 30 days, the provider must allow the customer to leave without an early exit fee.
Ofcom recommends Ethernet-connected testing for the most accurate speed measurement because Wi-Fi can reduce results.

guard_streams.source: Practical tips for improving your broadband speed

facts.detail: Distance from the exchange, time of day and simultaneous household use can affect broadband speed.
The guide recommends running several speed tests over multiple days and at different times.
Customers are advised to contact their provider first to diagnose connection problems.
Providers signed to the code commit to giving an estimated speed range in writing at contract start.
Code signatories allow customers to leave without penalty when speeds remain significantly below the original estimate.

guard_streams.source: What happens to your email address when you switch broadband provider

facts.detail: Ofcom states that it does not directly regulate email services.
A former broadband provider may charge customers who want to continue using a provider-issued email address.
Policies vary by provider, including free access, paid third-party access and account deletion.
The guide recommends considering a free independent webmail account to avoid being tied to a broadband provider.
Customers are advised to import contacts and messages, update important accounts, and configure forwarding or automatic replies.

guard_streams.source: Enforcement programme: Industry's failure to implement One Touch Switch by deadline of 3 April 2023

facts.detail: Ofcom opened the industry-wide enforcement programme on 3 April 2023.
The programme concerned General Conditions C7.18–C7.27 for residential broadband and landline switching.
One Touch Switch launched for most customers on 12 September 2024.
Ofcom concluded that most customers were successfully switching through One Touch Switch.
Ofcom closed the programme on 11 June 2026 while retaining ongoing compliance monitoring.

guard_streams.source: One million people have mapped their mobile – have you?

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Map Your Mobile milestone update on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used the checker.
The service accepts a postcode and maps available networks in the area.
The checker provides a score indicating which network performs best in the postal district.
The checker combines Opensignal crowdsourced experience data with predictive information from UK mobile networks.
